DURING THE DAY, SUNLIGHT ENTERS THE EARTH'S ATMOSPHERE AND INTERACTS WITH MOLECULES AND SMALL PARTICLES. RAYLEIGH SCATTERING OCCURS WHEN LIGHT WAVES INTERACT WITH PARTICLES MUCH SMALLER THAN THEIR WAVELENGTH. SHORTER WAVELENGTHS (BLUE/VIOLET) ARE SCATTERED MUCH MORE EFFICIENTLY THAN LONGER ONES (RED/YELLOW). THIS SCATTERED BLUE LIGHT IS DISTRIBUTED THROUGH THE ATMOSPHERE, REACHING OUR EYES FROM ALL DIRECTIONS, MAKING THE SKY APPEAR BLUE.

THE SHORTER WAVELENGTHS (BLUE) ARE SCATTERED OUT OF OUR LINE OF SIGHT, WHILE LONGER WAVELENGTHS (RED/ORANGE) TRAVEL THROUGH WITH LESS SCATTERING AND REACH OUR EYES. THIS MAKES THE SUN AND THE SKY APPEAR RED OR ORANGE.
